doc.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Pres calls him the slave: jazz slang explained
summary: Young said that if you have eyes the slave is yours; Haynes explains it meant you swing and the job is yours.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: That’s well documented. That history with you, and the use of the word “slave.” He said – what did he say?
Oh yeah. He wouldn’t hear that.
If you want to tell me. Whatever you want to be on the official record.

He thought I was swinging. He told me that after I played a couple tunes. He said, “You’re sure swinging Pres. If you have eyes, the slave is yours.” I stayed there two years. I hope that’s the last time I have to say that.
Okay. That will be the only time you have to say it here.

See, some people don’t know how he meant that, or they don’t know how he spoke. So when you start saying, or when it starts getting out, people say it, they say it wrong, say the wrong thing. A lot of the black musicians, they started a lot of the lingo that still is around now, that’s used on t.v. and all of these – a lot of the lingo came from the musicians. “Having eyes.” That was – a lot of the – what he meant is something you like. Say it to someone else, they don’t know what the hell you’re talking about. That’s why I hate to – I keep saying it over and over, and somebody gets this out of it. Then they say it. I say no, it wasn’t like that. It was like this. He meant, “You’re playing your ass off. You’re swinging. I like it. The job is yours.” We call – a job was a “slave.” I’m sure you know about that.
